subproblem.title: Mass measure of a finite-mass integer multiplicity current on ℝ^P, with integrality of its Borel restrictions
subproblem.statement: Assume, as hypotheses of the statement, (VO) (verbatim the antecedent (VO) of the selected statement): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) whose tsupport is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0; (MR) (verbatim the antecedent (MR) of the selected statement): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and IMRep R in U, if U is open and R represents T then M_W(T) = R.measure(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; and (IMC) (verbatim the antecedent (IMC) of the selected statement), the conjunction of (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces: for U open and Borel M ⊆ M′ ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M′ ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x and every subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ x Q; (b) for U open, an IMRep R in U and a Borel set E there are A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and an IMRep R′ in U representing A with R′.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R′.mult = R.mult and R′.orient = R.orient; (c) for U open, A − B is integer multiplicity whenever A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are; (d) for every IMRep R in U, for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x, |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α. Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity T: some IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of the contract represents T, i.e. T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, Hⁿ = μHE[n]) with M(T) < ∞. Then there are a measure μ on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n such that: (1) μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure); (2) ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; (3) for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α; (4) T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); (5) M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ ℝ^P; (6) μ(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0; (7) for every Borel set E ⊆ ℝ^P and every X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with X(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), X is integer multiplicity. Conventions (as in the frozen contract and SimonGMT Chapter06): ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)). For U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k; X(ω) is the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); 0 is the zero current; ∂X = X.boundary with ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply); currents with equal values are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). Λ_k = MultiVector P k (continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector). M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support = U \ X.zeroRegion, where X.zeroRegion is the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). Integrals ∫_E g dμ are Bochner integrals over μ⌞E; {d < t} abbreviates {x : d(x) < t}.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = R.measure W) → ((∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (E : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet E → ∃ (A : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R' : IMRep U n), R'.Represents A ∧ R'.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E ∧ R'.mult = R.mult ∧ R'.orient = R.orient) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsIntegerMultiplicity T → T.mass < ∞ → ∃ (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), IsFiniteMeasure μ ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) ∧ (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → T.massOn W = μ W) ∧ μ T.supportᶜ = 0 ∧ (∀ (E : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), MeasurableSet E → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, X ω = ∫ x in E, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 8 of the parent-supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtsd_shell_decomposition (the mass measure μ_T := R.measure and the integrality of the shells W_j); Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, §5, proof of the deformation theorem 5.1, displays (8)–(10) (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1725–1740). Siblings used: null_off_support (dimred_mbl_dtsd_sh_measure_compl_support_eq_zero) and IR = imrep_restriction (lcmp_imRep_measure_restrict: for every IMRep R in U, (a) R.measure ≪ Hⁿ⌞R.carrier, (b) R.orient is R.measure-a.e. strongly measurable, (c) for every Borel E and every IMRep R′ in U with R′.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R′.mult = R.mult and R′.orient = R.orient: R′.measure = R.measure⌞E and R′.action ω = ∫_E R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) for every form ω).
1. Since T is integer multiplicity, choose an IMRep R in ℝ^P (U = univ) representing T: T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Put μ := R.measure and ξ := R.orient.
2. ((5) and (1).) ℝ^P is open, so (MR) with U := ℝ^P gives M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, which is (5). For W := ℝ^P this gives μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(T) = M(T) < ∞ (T.mass is by definition T.massOn univ), so μ is a finite measure (IsFiniteMeasure.mk), which is (1).
3. ((2) and (3).) By IR (b), ξ = R.orient is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, which is (2). By (IMC)(d), for Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. x we have |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every n-covector α. By IR (a), μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞R.carrier, so every property holding Hⁿ⌞R.carrier-a.e. holds μ-a.e. (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le); this is (3).
4. ((4).) Apply IR (c) with the Borel set E := ℝ^P and R′ := R; its hypotheses R.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ℝ^P (Set.inter_univ), R.mult = R.mult and R.orient = R.orient hold. It gives R.action ω = ∫_{ℝ^P} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (setIntegral_univ) for every form ω. Since R represents T, T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), which is (4).
5. ((6).) By step 2, M_W(T) = μ(W) for every open W, so the sibling null_off_support, applied with (VO), X := T and μ, gives μ(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0, which is (6).
6. ((7).) Let E be Borel and X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with X(ω) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). By (IMC)(b) with U := ℝ^P (open), R and E there are A ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R′ with R′.carrier = R.carrier ∩ E, R′.mult = R.mult and R′.orient = R.orient (that R′ represents A is not needed). By IR (c) applied to E and R′, R′.action ω = ∫_E R.orient(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) = ∫_E ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = X(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). Hence R′ represents X, and X is integer multiplicity.
7. Steps 2–6 show that μ and ξ have properties (1)–(7). ∎

proof_key_steps: Choose an IMRep R of T; μ := R.measure, ξ := R.orient.
(MR) gives M_W(T) = μ(W) for open W, hence μ(ℝ^P) = M(T) < ∞ and μ is finite.
IR (a), (b) and (IMC)(d) give a.e. strong measurability of ξ and the μ-a.e. bound |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|.
IR (c) with E = ℝ^P, R′ = R gives T(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ.
null_off_support with (VO) gives μ(ℝ^P \ spt T) = 0.
(IMC)(b) gives an IMRep R′ with carrier R.carrier ∩ E; IR (c) shows R′.action = ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω), so X is IM.
